To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a semi-supervised offline RL method based on pre-training a decision transformer (DT) with a large amount of unlabelled data and fine-tuning it with small amount of task-specific data.

(1) pre-training a decision transformer on a large unlabelled dataset of expert demonstrations can be used to improve performance on downstream RL tasks, and (2) the pre-trained model can be further fine-tuned on a small labelled dataset of expert demonstrations, which can further improve performance.

(i) pre-training on a set of diverse tasks improves generalization to new ones; (ii) a single pre-training task is not always the best, and the choice depends on the target tasks; (iii) the choice of pre-training task can be learned from data, and this meta-learning of the pre-training task is a key component of our approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether pre-training can be used to improve the sample efficiency of offline RL, and if so, how.
the following questions: 1) Can we pre-train a deep RL model on large amounts of unlabeled data? 2) Can we fine-tune the pre-trained model on a small task-specific dataset?
developing a paradigm for RL, which is analogous to the success of transfer learning in CV and NLP.

the pre-training paradigm has not yet been successfully applied in the context of reinforcement learning, and it is still an active area of research.
the pre-training paradigm has been shown to improve the performance of RL agents in some cases and not in others.
pre-trained transformers are not a good choice for RL.

The main takeaway from our work is that

pre-training decision transformers (DTs) using large unlabeled datasets followed by fine tuning the DTs on small task-specific RL datasets can be a viable alternative to supervised offline reinforcement learning (RL) with expert demonstrations.
